text: When proving P(k+1), how does the induction hypothesis in strong (complete) induction differ from that in weak induction?
choices: It assumes P(m) holds for all m ≤ k, not merely P(k)
It assumes P(k+1) and derives P(k)
It drops the base case entirely
It assumes P(m) only for m > k
explanation: Strong (complete / course-of-values) induction assumes the entire history {P(m) : m ≤ k} rather than just the immediate predecessor P(k) — a stronger hypothesis useful when the recursion reaches back more than one step (as with Fibonacci bounds). It does not run backward, still uses a base case, and never assumes larger values.
